Hi @aojea , can you confirm that the stress test was running with this fixed code. From your tracing log, `		klog.LogToStderr(false)` is raced with klog's `output()`, but they are both protected by `logging.mu.Lock()`, this shouldn't happen.

In my local env, I haven't met this data race problem, at least so far.

> Hi @aojea , can you confirm that the stress test was running with this fixed code. From your tracing log, ` klog.LogToStderr(false)` is raced with klog's `output()`, but they are both protected by `logging.mu.Lock()`, this shouldn't happen.
> 
> In my local env, I haven't met this data race problem, at least so far.

I ran it with your PR, it took 9 mins to show the race ...

I'd like to explain several things:
1. I used to solve the problem by setting the `klog.LogToStderr(false)` 
first, then `os.Stderr.Write(data)` will not called at Line:1036, but I still can't figure out why @aojea still failed at the same code line as before since they're all protected by the mutex lock. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9e5efebb4c23a1926707e9faa80597602c09b45e/vendor/k8s.io/klog/v2/klog.go#L1035-L1036

2. Even I solved the potential data race at Line:1036, `os.Stderr.Write(data)` will still be called here as `s >= l.stderrThreshold.get()` is true here. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/debd461d03b0643ebcc34dc818c2f274d11b8817/vendor/k8s.io/klog/v2/klog.go#L1038-L1040

3. Since it's hard to control the `os` lib, then I changed the output with new defined buffer, then I can easily prevent from data race by using a Mutex RWLock.
But I still can't reproduce the data race problem in my local environment, will you @aojea kind to test this again when you have time?
